lines: Sixteen evenly spaced values between a start and an end voltage, each passed through a sine, then offset, scaled and taken modulo a chosen number, all sent out as one polyphonic cable
Sets the voltage the sixteen evenly spaced values begin at, over -10V to 10V
Sets the voltage the sixteen evenly spaced values end at, over -10V to 10V
Multiplies each of the sixteen values before the sine is taken, over -10 to 10, which sets how many cycles of the sine the span covers
Adds a constant to each sine result before it is scaled, over -10 to 10
Multiplies each offset sine result, over -10 to 10; at exactly 0 the sixteen values are never calculated and the output carries undefined data
Sets the number each value is taken modulo, over 0 to 10; a setting of 0 is treated as 0.001
Replaces the start knob with this voltage, so the knob does nothing while a cable is patched here and a cable resting at 0V sets the start to 0V
Replaces the end knob with this voltage, so the knob does nothing while a cable is patched here and a cable resting at 0V sets the end to 0V
Replaces the freq mult knob; a polyphonic cable gives each of the sixteen values its own multiplier, a monophonic one is used for all sixteen
Replaces the offset knob with this voltage, so the knob does nothing while a cable is patched here
Replaces the scale knob with this voltage; a cable resting at 0V leaves the output undefined
Replaces the modulus knob; a polyphonic cable gives each of the sixteen values its own modulus, a monophonic one is used for all sixteen
The sixteen calculated values, always sent as sixteen polyphonic channels
Note — Every input replaces its knob rather than adding to it, so patching a cable leaves that knob doing nothing until the cable is pulled.

pysgota.notes: Source read at commit c13145d, the last commit carrying version 2.0.2 with exactly the six installed models. SCALE at exactly 0 is a maker fault: pysgota.cpp:119 guards the whole loop with if (!(scale == 0)), so the local array range[16] at line 118 is left uninitialised and line 125 writes it to the output. lines: Converts a note voltage into the control voltage that sets the root note on various quantizer modules
The note taken as the root; only its pitch class is read, so the octave makes no difference
A voltage from 1V to 10.167V in twelve steps of 0.834V, which selects the root note on Bidoo's Dikt@t
A voltage from 0.84V to 10.01V in twelve steps of 0.834V, which selects the root note on quantizers with a twelve-step root control
Note — The maker's README names the quantizers the twelve output was tested against: JW-Modules Quantizer, NoteSeq and NoteSeq16, docB JTScaler, Alef's Bits Slips and SS-Modules Melodygen.
Note — Autinn's Fluencerator needs 5.83V subtracted from the twelve output before it will track, which the maker's README gives and the module does not do for you.
Note — Some quantizers take a note voltage as their root directly and need nothing from this module; the maker's README names Orange Line Mother and Grande Quant.

lines: Reads a value as a sixteen-bit binary number and puts each bit out as a gate on its own channel of a polyphonic cable, with a control that rotates which bit each channel takes
Sets the number that is converted to binary, over 0 to 9.9999 scaled so the full travel covers the sixteen bits; it starts at 0, which leaves every gate low
Rotates which bit each of the sixteen gate channels reads; the -10 to 10 travel covers one whole turn in each direction, but negative settings do not wrap
Replaces the value knob with this voltage, 0V to 10V covering the sixteen bits, so the knob does nothing while a cable is patched here
Replaces the shift knob with this voltage, 1.6 bits of rotation per volt, so the knob does nothing while a cable is patched here
Sixteen channels of gate, 10V where that bit of the value is set and 0V where it is not
Note — The sixteen lamps carry the same sixteen gates the polyphonic output does, one lamp per channel.
Note — The module comes up with its value at 0, so every gate is low and the output is silent until the value is turned up or a cable is patched into it.

clwyd.notes: Source read at commit c13145d. The shift is applied as x << ((s + i) % 16) at clwyd.cpp:86-104. For a negative shift that expression asks for a negative shift count, which C++ leaves undefined; built with clang on arm64 the affected channels read 0 rather than wrapping round, so the rotation is not symmetric about zero. clwyd.cpp:80 holds a commented-out shift_f * 16.f, the scaling the maker replaced with 1.6. The value input is not clamped, so voltages above 10V and below 0V reach the int conversion and set bits the knob cannot.

nilyniant.notes: Source read at commit c13145d. Neither output is rounded, so the voltage rises smoothly between notes rather than in steps; it is the receiving sequencer that quantises it to a sequence number.
